title: ai, ay
goal: Read and spell the long-a vowel team spelled **ai** (mid-word) and **ay** (end of word).

listen.passage: When trains are delayed during heavy rain, it is often because water can seep into the electrical system that controls the tracks, forcing a temporary shutdown until it is safe again.

tier2.def: lasting only for a short time, not permanent.
tier2.full: lasting only for a short time, not permanent.

questions: Why do trains sometimes stop running in heavy rain?
What's something in your life that was temporary but felt long?

A.text: It is play day at the park. / When rain starts, the class does not stay in — they play in the rain, and get wet from top to tail! / A snail comes on the wet path. / "There is a snail!" said Sam. / They wait for the rain to stop, then drink cold water and play again.

B.text: Every day, Kate takes the train to her job. / Today, because rain made the stop wet, the train came late. / She had to wait, so she got a cup of hot water and a snack from a stand. / "I will just wait," she said to a man in line. / The train came, and Kate got a spot by chance.
